content: Node plugin architecture: core exposes named extension points, a plugin manager owns discovery/loading/lifecycle, plugins implement a declared contract and register against hooks. Named precedents: Fastify plugins (encapsulation + lightweight DI via decorators), webpack Tapable (typed hook classes), ESLint plugin resolution (npm package naming convention + config-declared ordering), VS Code extensions. Practical guidance: declare the contract as a TS interface, load plugins as separate modules resolved by config-declared id, and never let plugin code share mutable core state.
